rules.quote: If memory and the docs ever disagree, the docs win and the memory is stale.
rules.rule: When the agent's memory files and the project docs (CLAUDE.md and docs/) disagree, follow the docs and treat the memory as stale.

rules.quote: Read the repo, do not reconstruct from memory
rules.rule: For the Astera Online project, read the repository files (CLAUDE.md, docs) rather than reconstructing product mission, decisions, balance numbers, or current state from memory.

rules.quote: read `CLAUDE.md` first, then `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/balance.md`
rules.rule: Before doing anything in the Astera Online repo, read CLAUDE.md first, then docs/decisions.md and docs/balance.md.

rules.quote: Those files are the source of truth and outrank anything remembered here.
rules.rule: Treat the blindspace repo docs as the source of truth over this memory file when they conflict.

rules.quote:
Do **not** reopen settled
design questions, keep improving the GDD, or restart the interview format.
rules.rule: Do not reopen settled design questions, keep improving the GDD, or restart the design-interview format for Astera Online.

rules.quote: The next job is a thin React client, deliberately not the 3D map.
rules.rule: Focus Astera Online execution work on building a thin React client, not the 3D map.

rules.quote: consult ~/Desktop/Coding/MyProjects/game-dev-handbook before every game-facing change and apply the principles that fit Astera
rules.rule: Before every game-facing change, consult the game-dev-handbook and apply the principles that fit Astera.

rules.quote: if the handbook covers the topic, follow it, as long as it suits Astera and makes the game better.
rules.rule: When the game-dev handbook covers the topic, follow its principles only if they suit Astera and make the game better.

rules.quote: open `README.md`, use the routing table, read the matching chapter.
rules.rule: Before working on a game task, open the handbook's README.md, use its routing table to find the matching chapter, and read that chapter.

rules.quote: Before delivery: run the matching section of `checklists.md`.
rules.rule: Before delivering game work, run the matching section of the handbook's checklists.md.

rules.quote: Cite the principle IDs used in the plan and the delivery note.
rules.rule: Cite the handbook principle IDs used in the plan and in the delivery note.

rules.quote: Action-game principles (coyote time, frame data, hit stop, parry) apply only to real-time surfaces such as Komutan Gemisi / Savaş Alanı.
rules.rule: Apply action-game principles (coyote time, frame data, hit stop, parry) only to real-time surfaces such as Komutan Gemisi / Savaş Alanı.

rules.quote: CLAUDE.md, docs/ and owner decisions outrank the handbook.
rules.rule: When handbook principles conflict with CLAUDE.md, docs/, or owner decisions, follow CLAUDE.md, docs/, or the owner's decisions over the handbook.

rules.quote: If a handbook principle would improve the game but clashes with a rule, present it as a trade-off and ask
rules.rule: If a handbook principle would improve the game but clashes with a rule, present it to the owner as a trade-off and ask before proceeding.

rules.quote: Do not present `Elaboration` or `Claimed, unverified` entries as proof.
rules.rule: Do not present handbook entries marked `Elaboration` or `Claimed, unverified` as proof.

rules.quote: Never implement the ML-05 anti-patterns without the owner's written approval.
rules.rule: Never implement the ML-05 anti-patterns without the owner's written approval.

rules.quote: **Everything typed.** `any` is banned. No casts to silence the compiler.
rules.rule: Type everything in the code; never use `any`, and never use casts to silence the compiler.

rules.quote: **A linter must be set up**, and its output must be zero.
rules.rule: Set up a linter on projects and ensure its output is zero before considering work done.

rules.quote:
If a rule is wrong, change the
  rule deliberately — never learn to ignore it.
rules.rule: If a lint rule is wrong, change the rule deliberately; never learn to ignore the linter's output.

rules.quote: **Every piece of code gets tests**
rules.rule: Write tests for every piece of code.

rules.quote:
tests must deliberately cover **edge cases**, not
  just the happy path: boundaries, malformed input, adversarial input, concurrency, failure,
  time.
rules.rule: Write tests that deliberately cover edge cases (boundaries, malformed input, adversarial input, concurrency, failure, time), not just the happy path.

rules.quote: **When writing or fixing a test, find the root cause first.**
rules.rule: When writing or fixing a test, find the root cause first.

rules.quote: tests must not be forced to fit the code.
rules.rule: Do not force tests to fit the code; establish whether the test or the code is wrong before changing either.

rules.quote: run typecheck + lint + tests as one gate before claiming anything is done.
rules.rule: Run typecheck, lint, and tests as one gate before claiming anything is done.

rules.quote: When several tests fail identically, that is one bug, not many.
rules.rule: When several tests fail identically, treat it as one bug, not many.

rules.quote:
When a test is flaky —
e.g. betting on a probabilistic roll — that is a defect to fix, not noise to tolerate.
rules.rule: Treat a flaky test (e.g. one relying on a probabilistic roll) as a defect to fix, not noise to tolerate.

rules.quote:
default behaviour is to move it
forward
rules.rule: When the user says a project is out of the design phase, move it forward by default through IMPLEMENT → TEST → PLAY → EVALUATE → FIX → CONTINUE.

rules.quote:
Decide yourself, without asking:** architecture, folder structure, library choice, query optimisation, caching, component design, internal API shape, test design, small UX details,
naming, refactors.
rules.rule: Decide architecture, folder structure, library choice, query optimisation, caching, component design, internal API shape, test design, small UX details, naming, and refactors yourself, without asking the user.

rules.quote:
**Ask only when** a change alters the core loop, the risk/reward structure, the product's
identity, or a decision already marked locked.
rules.rule: Ask the user only when a change alters the core loop, the risk/reward structure, the product's identity, or a decision already marked locked.

rules.quote: re-researching settled questions
rules.rule: Do not re-research settled questions.

rules.quote:
endlessly improving design
documents
rules.rule: Do not endlessly improve design documents.

rules.quote: waiting for every uncertainty to resolve before building
rules.rule: Do not wait for every uncertainty to resolve before building.

rules.quote:
approval requests for
small technical choices
rules.rule: Do not request approval for small technical choices.

rules.quote: redesigning a working system because something better might exist
rules.rule: Do not redesign a working system because something better might exist.

rules.quote: treating feature count as progress
rules.rule: Do not treat feature count as progress.

rules.quote:
never quietly drop or simplify core
gameplay because it is hard to build.
rules.rule: Never quietly drop or simplify core gameplay because it is hard to build.

rules.quote:
Ask instead what the simplest version is that
preserves the intended experience.
rules.rule: When core gameplay is hard to build, ask the user what the simplest version is that preserves the intended experience, instead of dropping or simplifying it.

rules.quote:
"simplified gameplay" is
a product decision that must be deliberate and stated.
rules.rule: Simplify gameplay only as a deliberate, stated product decision.

rules.quote:
Deliverables
and documentation stay in English.
rules.rule: Write deliverables and documentation in English.

rules.quote: when stuck, pick the smallest reversible option and continue.
rules.rule: When stuck, pick the smallest reversible option and continue.

rules.quote: Report what changed and what is next
rules.rule: Report what changed and what is next after completing work.

rules.quote: do not narrate every decision
rules.rule: Do not narrate every decision.
